text:
customer.tom: Hey team, since ~03:10 UTC our service in corp VPC fails mTLS to the Redwood Private control plane. App logs show repeated 'sslv3 alert handshake failure' and status code 525. No cert rotations on our side. Host: control.private.redwood.svc:443.

leah_support: sorry you're hitting this — we'll help debug. Can you paste an openssl s_client dump and confirm if you route through a corporate TLS proxy / NGFW? Also any recent DNS changes?

customer.tom: quick outputs below. We do have an outbound TLS-inspection proxy (corp-ngfw).

customer.tom: ```bash
# from app host
openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.svc:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile root_ca.pem -servername control.private.redwood.svc -showcerts -debug
CONNECTED(00000003)
3040:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:s3_pkt.c:1487:SSL alert number 40
---
No peer certificate available
---
```

mike_infra: thanks — two quick observations:
1) The s_client error and 'No peer certificate' suggest the TLS server never completed the handshake or the proxy terminated it.
2) Can you capture the TCP flow or share a packet capture showing ClientHello? If the corporate proxy is intercepting, it may be presenting a proxy cert and not forwarding the client cert (breaking mTLS).

customer.tom: grabbed tcpdump from the instance for a single failed attempt. Extract:```
13:10:02.123456 IP 10.2.3.4.53712 > 203.0.113.45.443: Flags [S], seq 12345, win 64240
13:10:02.223456 IP 203.0.113.45.443 > 10.2.3.4.53712: Flags [R], seq 0, ack 12346, win 0
```
Looks like RST from 203.0.113.45 (corporate egress gateway).

anil_network: that RST is telling — your DNS resolves control.private.redwood.svc to an egress-proxied IP (203.0.113.45). The corp NGFW is doing TLS-inspection and actively resetting flows that present client certs or unknown SNI. Many NGFWs will RST or terminate mTLS because they inject their own certs and don't pass client certs to backend.

leah_support: can you also paste the certificate the client expects (subject/issuer) and the SANs for the control plane server? Our control plane publishes certs with CN=control.private.redwood and SANs for the internal endpoints. If your proxy rewrites SNI or truncates it, the server will reject the handshake.

mike_infra: common pitfalls we see:
- TLS/HTTP proxy doing termination (breaks mTLS)
- SNI rewriting or truncation (long FQDNs get truncated by old proxies)
- Egress allowlist only permitting public FQDNs / specific SNI values
- Client not presenting cert or using wrong client cert chain

leah_support: please run these checks from an app host and paste outputs:
1) DNS resolution: `dig +short control.private.redwood.svc`
2) openssl with -servername and without to compare:
```
openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.svc:443 -servername control.private.redwood.svc -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile root_ca.pem -debug
openssl s_client -connect control.private.redwood.svc:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile root_ca.pem -debug
```
3) tcpdump during the attempt to see ClientHello bytes (look for SNI).

customer.tom: ran the dig: `203.0.113.45` (that's the corp proxy). When I hit the actual public IP we were given earlier (52.84.22.11) the handshake makes progress but the proxy rewrites.

customer.tom: I also tried `openssl s_client -connect 52.84.22.11:443 -servername control.private.redwood.svc -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile root_ca.pem -debug` and got a proper cert chain back from Redwood (subject CN=control.private.redwood, SAN includes control.private.redwood.svc). But hitting the proxied IP fails.

anil_network: that confirms it — proxy is the blocker. Two remediation paths:
- Preferred: configure corp NGFW to do TCP passthrough (no TLS-inspection) for the control plane IPs and port 443, or add an allowlist rule for the FQDN/IP where inspection is disabled. mTLS requires end-to-end TLS.
- Alternative: terminate TLS at the proxy and forward client cert info via headers to the backend — not supported by our private control plane (we require true mTLS).

mike_infra: for the customer's network team, here's a checklist to hand them:
- Allow outbound TCP 443 to 52.84.22.11 and other control plane IPs (provided in your onboarding doc).
- Disable TLS inspection for those IPs/FQDNs.
- Ensure SNI is forwarded intact. Some older proxies truncate SNI > 64 chars — consider short-names if you can't change the proxy.
- If using explicit proxy, ensure CONNECT tunnels raw TCP (not terminating TLS).

leah_support: I've opened an internal ticket and flagged network eng. infra-bot created RED-7892 and linked the customer's case.

infra-bot: Created ticket RED-7892 and attached initial tcpdump and s_client outputs. https://redwood.support/RED-7892

sre_oncall: scheduling a troubleshooting call with customer and their network team at 11:00 UTC. Please join: meets://redwood/RED-7892-call

customer.tom: FYI — I asked our network team to add a passthrough rule for 52.84.22.11 and disable TLS inspection for that IP. After change we retried and it worked.

customer.tom: quick verification output: ```
# now works
openssl s_client -connect 52.84.22.11:443 -servername control.private.redwood.svc -cert client.pem -key client.key -CAfile root_ca.pem -showcerts
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=control.private.redwood
 1 s:/CN=Redwood Control CA
---
SSL handshake has read 4153 bytes and written 305 bytes
Verification: OK
```

leah_support: great to hear! Marking as resolved pending postmortem. Action items:
- Customer to keep passthrough allowlist in place for control plane IPs.
- We will add clearer guidance to onboarding docs calling out TLS-inspection as incompatible with Private mTLS.

mike_infra: also adding a note to the onboarding IP list: request customers confirm their NGFW supports TLS passthrough for mTLS endpoints.

customer.tom: thanks everyone :rocket: — please keep RED-7892 open until we run a final postmortem.

leah_support: will do. Closing the Slack thread but ticket remains open.
